ai-code-reviewer.title: AI Code Reviewer
ai-code-reviewer.tagline: AI-powered GitHub Pull Request review, with Java test generation
ai-code-reviewer.summary: An automated analysis platform for GitHub Pull Requests. For each Pull Request, it examines the changes in the context of the rest of the codebase, relies on a language model to detect issues, then posts contextual comments directly on the affected lines. It can also generate Java unit tests and run them in a Docker sandbox.
features: Automatic review of GitHub Pull Requests, with inline comments ranked by severity
Code context analysis beyond the changes alone: Tree-sitter syntax analysis and similar-code search with embeddings (pgvector)
Static analysis with Semgrep, combined with the language model’s findings
Java unit test generation (JUnit 5, Mockito) for modified methods, compiled and run in a network-isolated Docker sandbox
Interchangeable model providers (Gemini, Claude, OpenRouter, OpenAI-compatible API), with automatic fallback to a second provider
Asynchronous processing of reviews and indexing (Redis, BullMQ), with step-by-step tracking in a dashboard
MCP server: run a review of your local changes from Claude Code

items: Docker sandbox: compilation and JUnit 5 / Mockito tests
Reports published on GitHub Pull Requests

ai-code-reviewer.role: A university team project organized into five modules. I developed the Java test generation in a Docker sandbox, the analysis optimization, the asynchronous processing and the automated tests.
contributions: Java test generation pipeline: context extraction with Tree-sitter, LLM-generated JUnit 5 / Mockito tests, secure compilation and execution in a Docker sandbox.
Analysis optimization: Semgrep, routing between the Gemini and Claude models and a PostgreSQL cache based on SHA-256 to limit LLM calls and token consumption.
Asynchronous processing with Redis and BullMQ, NestJS REST API and automatic publication of reports on GitHub Pull Requests.
Automated tests with Vitest and E2E tests with Katalon Recorder (Selenium).

alzheimer-ehealth.title: E-health platform for Alzheimer’s risk detection
alzheimer-ehealth.tagline: Daily assistance microservice and real-time notifications
alzheimer-ehealth.summary: A microservices-based platform to monitor patients with Alzheimer’s disease and detect at-risk situations in real time. It offers spaces tailored to each role (administrator, doctor, carer, family caregiver, patient), with centralized authentication. Project carried out at ESPRIT as part of the PIDEV program (4th year).
features: Role-based access (administrator, doctor, carer, family caregiver, patient) with centralized Keycloak authentication (OAuth2/OIDC)
Doctor dashboard: patients followed, today’s appointments, pending reports, medical and critical alerts
Cognitive risk assessment from demographic data, lifestyle and cognitive scores, using a decision tree classifier
Day-to-day care follow-up: medical reports, visual agenda and handover sheets, with weekly reports validated by the carer then sent to the doctor
Management of users and care-network profiles, with distribution and registration statistics
Microservices architecture: single entry point through an API Gateway and dynamic service discovery (Eureka)
Automated delivery pipeline: Jenkins pipelines, Docker images published to Nexus, Kubernetes deployment and Prometheus/Grafana monitoring
alzheimer-ehealth.role: A team project carried out at ESPRIT. I developed the Daily Assistance microservice, its integration with the other services, the real-time notifications and the related Angular interfaces, and contributed to the DevOps pipeline.
contributions: Development of the Daily Assistance microservice: REST API, medical reports, assisted memory and handover sheets.
Integration of the microservice with the other services through OpenFeign and RabbitMQ.
Real-time notifications via WebSocket (STOMP/SockJS) and Angular interfaces.
Contribution to the DevOps pipeline (Docker, Jenkins CI/CD, Nexus, Kubernetes, SonarQube, Prometheus/Grafana) and tests with JUnit and Mockito.

shots.caption: Doctor dashboard: appointment tracking, cognitive alerts and patient metrics.
Clinical risk evaluation computed via Decision Tree Classifier.
Weekly care records tracking and medical consolidation.
Account administration: caregiver and patient distribution with permissions.
Real-time metrics of microservice containers on Kubernetes cluster.
Automated continuous integration and deployment for microservices.

digifederation.title: DigiFederation
digifederation.tagline: School and university sports management platform on microservices (PFA internship, ESPRIT DSI)
digifederation.summary: DigiFederation is a school and university sports management platform for a Tunisian federation, built by seven teams with distinct scopes. My team was responsible for the Finance / Licences / Competitions scope: licence applications and the digital licence, competitions, matches and rankings. Project carried out during my PFA internship at ESPRIT’s Information Systems Department, and being prepared for production.
features: Licences: application with supporting documents (ID card, photo, medical certificate, parental authorization), document review with approval or reasoned rejection, application status tracking
Official digital licence: card showing category, club, season and QR code, exportable as PDF
Competitions: tracking by status (registration open, ongoing, finished), discipline, season and venue
Match schedule and match sheets entered in the referee space (scores, attendance, goals, cards), with rankings calculated automatically and published when the competition closes
Participation commitments: number of teams per institution, sport and category for the season
Access by role and scope (general supervisor, regional delegate, association manager, teacher, student)
Other scopes, built by other teams: authentication and users, members and clubs, communication and documents, statistics, website and mobile application
digifederation.role: Scrum Master of the Finance / Licences / Competitions team (6 members), one of the project’s seven scopes, and backend developer within that team.
contributions: Scrum Master: team coordination, Sprint Backlog follow-up, unblocking issues and coordinating the integration of the services.
Development of the Competitions module with NestJS and MongoDB: registrations, participant eligibility, fields and referees, schedules and rankings.
Design and configuration of the Node.js API Gateway: routing to the microservices and CORS handling.
Contribution to the Finance and Licences modules, with inter-service integration via HTTP/REST and RabbitMQ.
digifederation.context: This institutional project developed for the Tunisian School and University Sports Federation was officially honored during the closing ceremony at ESPRIT, with an honorary trophy and certificate of merit.
